title: Rapid triage template and rubric for optimization/advisory requests (batching, cache, quantization, routing)
creator: Amrita Kapoor
description: Create a concise, repeatable triage template and scoring rubric to classify incoming optimization/advisory requests (non-bug) about batching, caching, quantization, and routing policies. The goal is to reduce time-to-first-response, increase correct routing to self-serve vs. engineering advisory lanes, and capture signals for product improvements. This ticket delivers the template, an example filled intake, routing matrix, and onboarding notes for Solutions/Support teams.
acceptance_criteria: Published triage intake template available to Support and Solutions as a Google Form + Confluence doc
Scoring rubric with numeric weights for impact, risk, effort, and strategic value documented
Routing matrix mapping score ranges to lanes: Self-serve guide, Optimization Concierge (PM+SE consult), Engineering Advisory (Eng ETA + Dedicated work), or Enterprise Escalation (Sales/CS + SLA)
Two representative, anonymized example requests filled out and routed with rationales
Handoff checklist for engagements (required artifacts, SSO/access, contact list) added to Confluence
Stakeholder review recorded: Product, Solutions, Eng, and Support signoffs
proposed_workflow: 1) Intake submission by customer or internal rep with required workload signals. 2) Automated pre-score based on form fields (simple weights) + manual quick-triage by Solutions within 3 business days. 3) Route to lane based on score. 4) For Advisory lanes, create PM ticket and attach runbook; for Engineering lanes, create ENG ticket with required reproduction bundle. 5) Record outcome and update scoring model monthly.
scoring_rubric: Impact (0-10): expected cost savings or latency reduction for critical paths. 7-10 = high (enterprise SLA or >30% cost saving), 4-6 = medium, 0-3 = low
Risk (0-10): risk of quality regression or customer data exposure from changes (quantization, routing). Higher risk increases engineering oversight requirement
Effort (0-10): rough engineering/SE effort estimate to deliver recommendations or changes (0-3 trivial, 4-7 moderate, 8-10 large)
Strategic value (0-5): alignment with roadmap or strategic customers (integrations, enterprise commitments)
routing_matrix: Score <= 8: Self-serve lane (formal recommendation doc + automated knob suggestions). Owner: Support + Docs
Score 9-15: Optimization Concierge (PM + SE 2-week engagement). Owner: Solutions + PM
Score 16-23: Engineering Advisory (Eng + PM, timeboxed spike and RFC). Owner: Eng + PM
Score >=24 OR customer_requested-SLA: Enterprise Escalation (Sales/CS + dedicated SLAs). Owner: Sales/CS + Platform Eng
intake_required_fields: Use case description and business impact
Traffic profile (QPS, avg tokens/request, peak tokens/sec)
Observed latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) and request/response examples
KV cache hit-rate or prefix reuse signal
Token cost per 1M and monthly spend estimate
Tolerance for quality delta (numeric threshold or qualitative)
Access (logs, example requests, test keys) and legal constraints
escalation_playbook: If request flags customer_impact = high, notify Customer Success within 2 hours and assign Enterprise Escalation lane
If security_review_required = true, pause implementation and start security review process (SecurOps) before engineering changes
For high-risk quantization requests, require a canary rollout + quality regression set locked as part of the advisory
For cross-region routing changes, require network/security signoff and a rollback plan
notes_and_decisions: Decision 2025-02-16: Use a simple additive numeric rubric for first iteration (weights: Impact 0.5, Risk 0.2, Effort 0.2, Strategic 0.1)
Trade-off: Keep initial automation lightweight to avoid false positives; human-in-the-loop triage is mandatory for scores in 9-23
Follow-up: Build a telemetry schema to capture outcomes (post-change latency, cost delta, quality regression) to refine weights after 6 weeks
We will keep the Support intake verbatim fields to preserve evidence for audits and replay
